mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to equities, thereby lowering the present value of future cash flows and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses and remains above 5.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero under the same inflation regime (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS reverts below 5.25% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 1.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months indicates labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 1.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal, or the PAYEMS growth rate reverts below 1.5% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer demand proxies such as HOUST (units sold) exceeding 2% month-over-month triggers inventory drawdowns and production acceleration, which lift investor confidence and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > +2% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the HOUST signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO index < 100 for two consecutive months) suggests supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and elevates risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO index remains below 100 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified slowdown period.

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it indicates a labor market softening that reduces the real rate of return to equity investments, thereby pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative or do not diverge from a baseline model (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE cooling period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS and RSAFS (both rising > 2% MoM) signals a dual labor and demand expansion that supports corporate earnings momentum and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both increase by more than 2% in the same month
regime_hint: dual labor demand and supply expansion
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when both labor indicators are strong (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in CPIAUCSL exceeding 0.3% month-over-month followed by two consecutive months above 0.4% indicates aggressive price inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher rates and depressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in one month, then > 0.4% in the next two months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative or do not show a statistically significant decline (p > 0.05) during the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: When the product of INDPRO and GDPC1 falls by more than 5% quarter-over-quarter, it reflects simultaneous supply contraction and demand weakness, raising uncertainty and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified imbalance period.
